people.name: John de Glasgu / Glasgw of Stirling
people.summary: Selected uncertain identity: the Glasgow burgess of 1447–1455 and Stirling witness of 1475–1480 are modelled as one man. Both source groups remain separate and intact. A compatible 33-year adult career and shared civic role favour this provisional model; father–son and other-family alternatives remain open. Birth and death unknown. His two selected uncertain father links remain conditional, with no additional parent or component-join credit.

identity_selection.basis: Select the Glasgow burgess of 1447–1455 and the Stirling witness of 1475–1479/80 as the same man, at low confidence. Both groups use compatible John de Glasgu/Glasgw name forms in burgh-property witnessing, and the August 1475 catalogue places the Stirling John among burgesses. An adult active in 1447 could still witness in 1480 in his fifties or older. The conventional circa-1450 Stirling birth was inferred from an assumed young adult in 1475; it cannot establish a second man. A single compatible civic career is the simpler working model than inserting another generation from that estimate.
identity_selection.limitations: No shared holding, relative, trade, personal seal or distinctive repeated associate joins the cities. The Glasgow-to-Stirling change is not itself evidence of migration. Father–son, other kin and two unrelated namesakes remain viable alternatives. The name may still be a personal byname; this selection does not prove hereditary surname transmission. The two Glasgow acts remain one high-confidence group and the three Stirling acts another; only their cross-group identity is selected uncertain. No birth, death or additional parent is inferred.
identity_selection.prior_assessment: Two separate documentary accounts; compatible identity and father–son alternatives, neither selected.

Its truncated surname string ASGOWE is retained in the profile comparison, not silently expanded as an original-image reading. The old exact-looking birth year is displayed as circa 1610, an inherited estimate with no age record. South Leith is the marriage place, not an evidenced death place; death date and place remain unknown. The 24 April 1665 date belongs to Jonet Cowan’s testament-index entry, not Matthew’s birth, marriage or death. No original source was newly inspected.

chronology.reason: The Dublin records name no Scottish parents, birthplace or apprenticeship, so the Scottish child and elder watchmaker may be different men. The fresh Glasco-146 biography itself mixes the 1752 watchmaker with junior notices of 1765,1768 and 1770. Its c.1715 birth and the c.1740 birth of Glasco-147 are tree estimates, not evidence selecting a generation. If Glasco-146 instead represents the junior, the elder Philip is an alternative father-generation placement and the Thomas link would need revision; no competing father is attached alongside it. The elder placement is a preferred working interpretation of the profile’s trade/address and family structure, not a claim that every event in that biography belongs to him. The junior’s 1765 unnamed-wife death,1768 Teresa Plunkett marriage and reported 1770 death remain with the younger documentary account Glasgow-3932. Glasco-147 is a strongly supported duplicate account of that younger man, but its quoted 1772 younger/inventory wording was not independently rechecked here and establishes neither the estimated birth nor a newly verified father clause; a grant date is not a death date. No merge, spouse transfer or new child attachment follows. Catherine Mangan is called Glasco-146’s mother in its prose but spouse in its structured family; the 1750 report describes the elder’s bride only as the widow Mangan, and the 1760 report gives no forename. Neither record proves maternity. Preserve the existing Mangan/Braccan and younger-parent fields as qualified leads; do not add a mother for Glasco-146. The father Thomas is common to the retained 1711 child records, while the 3 June Uphall versus 21 October Linlithgow Philip entries and their maternal readings remain unreconciled; Jean Duncan is not transferred as Glasco-146’s mother. The 1777 probate/court occurrence does not establish survival after 1772. The local elder account uses 1772 as an uncertain death year through the selected identity, retaining the old after 1772 value and all junior events in the comparison.

death.qualifier: Reported elder watchmaker death; identification with this account remains selected uncertain. The 1777 probate occurrence does not establish survival.

chronology.reason: The former local circa 1766 birth for Hartshorne-320 was generated as 18 years before her 1784 death, as the imported record’s own note explains. It was not a birth date supplied by the captured profile, which leaves the date empty. It also conflicts with the existing mid-century children and the Cecil probate-family account. The local birth display is corrected to Unknown, retaining the old derived value in the imported comparison. No replacement birth year is invented; Cecil County remains her inherited, uncertain birthplace. This correction is separate from the new parent hypothesis and does not prove Robert’s maternity.
